notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR5: "Integer-1 or the value of the data item referenced by identifier-3 may be zero", the explicit allowance the integer definition asks for (an integer in a format "must be neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed by the rules for that format", §1985:III.2). sendAdvancingPhrase admits integerLiteral or a literal, and ScreenSendAdvancing refuses every literal but the figurative ZERO (any spelling, with or without ALL); identifier-3's value is not screened, so zero runs. Witness compiles 0 LINES and a zero identifier unexecuted. Probes at --std 85: (f) 0 LINES, 00 LINE, ZERO, ZEROS, ZEROES, ALL ZERO, PIC 9 and S9(3) holding 0 accepted and, executed, sent the message (00); 9(18) of all nines ran; (b) -1, +2, -0, 1.0, "2", SPACE, QUOTE, ALL "0" refused COBOL6171; an 18-digit literal is refused COBOL2427 under the documented 2,147,483,647 implementation limit (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3).

next.reason: 1985: "Integer-1 or the value of the data item referenced by identifier-3 may be zero."; 2023: "SEND now sends to a message server run unit (SR-14.9.38.3-2); the communication module's SEND with ADVANCING integer is gone". The 1985 rule allows a zero ADVANCING count in the communication SEND. The 2023 SEND is a message-server statement with no ADVANCING phrase, so the requirement is dropped.
